record.context_brief: BKM test question: conservation laws and symmetries
record.original_question: For a candidate integrable PDE system, what is the structure of its conservation laws and symmetries, and does it match the BKM pattern in which conservation laws have even order and symmetries have odd order?

evidence.quote: TQ2 What do the conservation laws and symmetries look like? (In the BKM-systems, the orders of the conservation laws are even, and of symmetries are odd)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A Nijenhuis operator on a smooth manifold $M$ is a $(1,1)$-tensor field $L$ whose Nijenhuis torsion
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]$$
vanishes for all vector fields $X,Y$. Out of such operators one constructs a distinguished class of multicomponent quasilinear evolutionary PDE systems, called BKM systems, which include (for one component) the KdV, Harry Dym, Camassa–Holm and Dullin–Gottwald–Holm equations, and (for several components) the Kaup–Boussinesq, coupled Harry Dym, coupled KdV and multi-component Camassa–Holm equations. A symmetry of an evolutionary system $u_t = F(u,u_x,u_{xx},\dots)$ is an evolutionary vector field $u_\tau = G(u,u_x,\dots,\partial_x^k u)$ commuting with the flow; its order is the largest $k$ such that $\partial G/\partial(\partial_x^k u)\neq 0$. A conservation law is a pair $(\rho,\sigma)$ with $D_t \rho = D_x \sigma$ on solutions, and its order is the highest order of $x$-derivatives appearing in the density $\rho$ (modulo total $x$-derivatives).

Problem. Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a candidate integrable evolutionary PDE system associated with a Nijenhuis operator (a putative BKM system). 

(a) Describe the algebraic and differential structure of the full hierarchy of local conservation laws and the hierarchy of local higher symmetries of $\mathcal{S}$ in terms of the underlying Nijenhuis operator.

(b) Prove or disprove that $\mathcal{S}$ obeys the BKM parity pattern: every local conservation law of $\mathcal{S}$ has even order, and every local higher symmetry of $\mathcal{S}$ has odd order. Identify necessary and sufficient conditions on the Nijenhuis data under which this even/odd pattern holds.
artifact.category_tag: Nijenhuis geometry and BKM integrable systems
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as one of the test questions ("TQ2") in a recent collection of research problems on BKM systems arising from Nijenhuis geometry. The parity pattern (even-order conservation laws, odd-order symmetries) is observed empirically for known BKM examples (KdV, Harry Dym, Camassa–Holm, Kaup–Boussinesq, etc.), and a related study of conservation laws and symmetries for non-diagonalisable hydrodynamic-type systems exists, but no general structural theorem establishing the pattern for all BKM systems has been published. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: TQ2 What do the conservation laws and symmetries look like? (In the BKM-systems, the orders of the conservation laws are even, and of symmetries are odd)
status_evidence.claim: The parity pattern is stated as an empirical observation and posed as an open test question.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry IV: conservation laws, symmetries and integration of certain non-diagonalisable systems of hydrodynamic type
status_evidence.snippet: Conservation laws and symmetries for non-diagonalisable hydrodynamic systems associated with Nijenhuis operators.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on conservation laws/symmetries for related Nijenhuis systems exist but do not establish the general BKM parity pattern.

status_evidence.title: Lax pairs for BKM hierarchy
status_evidence.snippet: Lax pair construction for the BKM hierarchy; further structural study of these systems is ongoing.
status_evidence.claim: Structural study of BKM hierarchies is an active area without a definitive resolution of the parity question.
